scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and "fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills."
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume doubled from a ~600/month baseline (610, 590) to 1180 (2026-08) and 1260 (2026-09) (E-07).
Majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) occur on bills carrying ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, meter reads (E-02).
Manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target, affecting 9200 manual-read accounts (E-01).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets doubled Aug-Sep 2026 (E-07) because, per the only surviving supported hypothesis (H-RULE-CHANGE), a change to billing import validation rules around August causes the billing system to compute or accept bills incorrectly on accounts with actual (non-estimated) meter reads, generating genuine billing errors that drive disputes. This is evidenced by disputed bills being dominated by ACTUAL-read bills (1785 of 3025, E-02), a pattern that estimate-substitution mechanisms (AMI vendor gaps, field manual-read gaps, staffing shortfall) cannot explain since they act only through estimate substitution, and it is not a response-speed problem since ticket response times are within the 3.0-day SLA (E-04).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-02 revised by E-11: E-02 still shows disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL (total 3025) — that observation is unchanged. It no longer supports the premise that a billing rule change causes ACTUAL-read bills to be computed/accepted incorrectly: E-11 confirms the only identified billing-import-rule mechanism (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) acts on AMI reads by rejecting good reads and forcing estimate substitution within the ESTIMATED population, not by miscomputing ACTUAL-read bills, so E-02's ACTUAL-majority split no longer rules in H-RULE-CHANGE's asserted causal pathway for PR-ROOT/PR-CHAIN-5.

F-01.statement: Manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1240 on ESTIMATED reads and 1785 on ACTUAL reads (total 3025).

F-04.statement: Dispute ticket response times: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA, across 2440 tickets.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes, which are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: A route-log query identified 14 lagging manual-read routes with distinct completion rates, e.g. route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

F-08.statement: Of 1240 AMI read events tied to disputed ESTIMATED bills, 1184 had an AMI read received before cutoff but were rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (still exported to billing), and 56 had no AMI read received at all (not exported).

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a customer-service response-capacity problem; auto-answering tickets would resolve it even without changing bill accuracy.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August is causing bills to be computed or accepted incorrectly, generating genuine billing errors.

H-AMI-DATA-GAP.statement: AMI read delivery/validation problems (vendor side) cause MDMS to miss or mis-validate interval reads, forcing more estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Manual field meter-read handoff failures (bad or missing reads from the contracted field service) are feeding incorrect data into billing, causing wrong bills.

H-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A field staffing shortfall caused missed/incomplete manual read routes since August, increasing estimated bills and disputes.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as high-consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution on otherwise-successfully-read accounts and driving disputes on that estimated-bill population.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route-log data (E-01) shows manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, affecting 9200 manual-read accounts — a shortfall in the field manual-read collection step of the meter-to-cash process during the dispute surge period.

E-02 shows disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL (total 3025); a clear majority of disputes occur on bills carrying an actual (not estimated) read. This limits how much any read-availability-gap theory (AMI vendor issues, field manual-read gaps, staffing) can explain, since those mechanisms act through estimate substitution and cannot account for the larger ACTUAL-read dispute population.

E-02 still shows disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL (total 3025) — that observation is unchanged. It no longer supports the premise that a billing rule change causes ACTUAL-read bills to be computed/accepted incorrectly: E-11 confirms the only identified billing-import-rule mechanism (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) acts on AMI reads by rejecting good reads and forcing estimate substitution within the ESTIMATED population, not by miscomputing ACTUAL-read bills, so E-02's ACTUAL-majority split no longer rules in H-RULE-CHANGE's asserted causal pathway for PR-ROOT/PR-CHAIN-5.

E-03 shows the billing-db tariff change log has zero entries, meaning no tariff/rate changes were made around the dispute surge period. This rules out a tariff-change explanation for the wrong-bill symptom, but it does not speak to the separate billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES/billing-config) that H-RULE-CHANGE actually concerns.

E-04 shows CRM dispute ticket response times (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are already within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, so slow response is not the operative problem for this ticket population regardless of the dispute surge.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims a three-reader staffing shortfall since July causes routes to run late, so affected customers get estimated bills. This is an unverified stakeholder claim from a source with disclosed incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias (attributes problems to staffing), and it adds no new quantified data beyond the already-recorded E-01 route completion shortfall.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's claim that there was no tariff change this year corroborates the already-recorded authoritative finding E-03 (tariff_change_log=0 records), but as an unverified stakeholder statement it adds no new quantified data. It does not speak to any of the five live wrong-bill hypotheses, none of which allege a tariff-change cause (H-RULE-CHANGE concerns import validation rules, not tariffs).

CRM dispute_volume_monthly (E-07, authoritative, complete) shows ticket counts of 610 (2026-06) and 590 (2026-07) baseline rising to 1180 (2026-08) and 1260 (2026-09), confirming the surge roughly doubled coincident with August. This validates the magnitude/timing of the surge framing but does not by itself indicate which causal mechanism (billing errors vs. response capacity) is responsible.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is a service-contract clause confirming that route priority changes are executed only after runtime confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD), formally corroborating the already-recorded K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint; it does not speak to billing dispute causation.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-09 is an authoritative, complete route-log query returning 14 distinct lagging routes with per-route completion values (e.g. route R-00 at 0.70), providing a route-level breakdown of the aggregate 0.88 shortfall already recorded in E-01. It does not link these routes/accounts to estimated vs actual read types or to disputed bills, so it does not by itself resolve whether the shortfall contributes to the dispute surge (VOB-R-3 / U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-RELEVANCE).

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI reports that vendor export access to MDMS for Lakeside is now provisioned (vendor ticket TX-4471), which if true would unblock the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query; this is a stakeholder claim about tooling access, not new causal evidence about the dispute surge.

This shows the dominant driver of ESTIMATED-bill disputes is a billing-import rejection on high-consumption reads, not an AMI vendor delivery gap.

structural_remedies.description: Run the already-scoped deterministic query of DA-RULES/billing-config for entries dated around August 2026 and cross-check timing against E-02's disputed-ACTUAL-read population.
structural_remedies.rationale: billing-config is a read-only AUTHORITATIVE tool already in intended_scope (investigate_billing_rule_change); no HUMAN_APPROVAL or AUTHORITY constraint governs read access, and 225 min remain though tool_health is UNKNOWN and may need retry.; residual gap: Confirms or refutes rule-change occurrence but does not by itself identify the specific defect or fix any wrong bills; VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRM remains until this returns legible dated entries (A-RULE-LOG-WILL-CONFIRM is still an assumption).

structural_remedies.description: Run a deterministic categorization query on DA-BILL for the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills using existing structured error/exception codes, if present, to answer U-ERROR-PATTERN.
structural_remedies.rationale: billing-db is HEALTHY and read-only AUTHORITATIVE; no constraint blocks the query, but DA-BILL completeness is UNKNOWN.; residual gap: If DA-BILL lacks structured error/exception fields, a deterministic query cannot classify error types (rate misapplication, duplicate charge, multiplier error, etc.), leaving VOB-U-ERROR-PATTERN unresolved.

structural_remedies.description: If #1 confirms a faulty rule, apply a config correction/rollback to the specific import validation rule through standard billing-config change management with SH-BILL sign-off.
structural_remedies.rationale: No cited constraint blocks a billing-config rule edit (K-BILLWRITE governs write_bill_adjustment specifically, not rule-config); routing through SH-BILL authority is prudent given CRITICAL unknown status and CONDITIONAL_PASS gate.; residual gap: Depends entirely on #1 producing a confirmed, specific defect; does not retroactively correct bills already issued incorrectly to customers.

structural_remedies.description: Design a Human-Gate-approved batch re-bill/credit workflow for accounts whose ACTUAL-read bills are confirmed erroneous, executed only by SH-BILL under K-BILLWRITE.
structural_remedies.rationale: K-BILLWRITE mandates no automated bill writes and requires Billing Operations approval per SC-NO-AUTOMATED-BILL-WRITE; the process can be designed now but full-scale execution across affected accounts likely exceeds the remaining 225 min / 30 min reserve.; residual gap: Cannot be scoped until U-ERROR-PATTERN identifies which accounts/bills are actually erroneous; addresses symptom (wrong bills already issued) not the generating cause.

structural_remedies.description: Introduce a mandatory pre-deployment review/sign-off and audit log requirement for billing-config import validation rule changes to prevent future silent, undetected rule changes.
